finding: Initialization cleared only 61 words, leaving achievement/task counters, current-frame sums and worst-frame snapshot data at later offsets stale when the profile marker was absent.
fix: Clear all 358 words used by the profile layout, including the final snapshot at indices 330..357.
verification: python scripts/check_overworld_profile.py; actual GNU ARM compilation with HACK_PROFILE enabled recorded in overworld_profile_arm.json
timer_sampling_fix: ProfNow reads vblankCounter2 through a const volatile u32 pointer both before and after the volatile scanline sample, preventing compiler reuse of a nonvolatile interrupt-updated counter read.
timer_verification: 233 cases: all 227 stable scanlines outside the ambiguous line 160, up to three simulated intervening frame updates, line-160 retry and UINT32_MAX frame arithmetic wrap. Actual HACK_PROFILE ARM object compilation passed; ProfNow was inlined, so no standalone symbol disassembly claim is made.
frame_base_fix: The callback previously sampled ProfNow then reread the frame counter separately; an intervening VBlank could make start-frameStart underflow. ProfSampleTime now optionally returns the frame base from the same stable counter/scanline pair; ProfNow wraps it for existing callers.
frame_base_verification: 908 cases covering 227 scanlines at four frame-counter seeds, including UINT32_MAX with two simulated intervening frame increments. Returned timestamp minus its associated frame base always equals the 0..227 scanline phase, including arithmetic wrap.
coverage: All 28 sections with zero, one, 228 and UINT32_MAX elapsed values. Starts with dirty storage and checks every initialized word, adjacent guard words, additive totals/current-frame sums, maxima, wraparound and preservation of initialized auxiliary counters on later calls.
limitations: Mocked memory clearing and profile buffer; no hardware timer, VBlank concurrency, full profiling callback or runtime/cycle benchmark verification.
